title: Denial Reasons and Appeals Reference, Host Damage Protection (HostCover)
content:
A **Host Damage Protection (HostCover)** claim is denied, with the matching denial reason recorded, in each of the situations below. A host may appeal a denial once, within the level's appeal window; the claims team's decision on the appeal is final.

## Denial reasons

| Denial reason recorded | The claim is denied when |
|---|---|
| filed late | it was filed after the filing window |
| no guest request | no payment request was sent to the guest first |
| excluded damage | the damage is excluded: ordinary wear and tear, cash or securities, vehicles or watercraft, damage present before the stay, or damage caused by the host or the host's staff |
| insufficient evidence | the claim lacks the evidence the level requires |
| coverage inactive | the stay did not check in under an active plan |
| below minimum | the claimed amount is below the level's minimum claimed amount |
| claim limit reached | the plan year's paid-claim count is used up |
| not escalated in time | the host did not escalate in time |

## Related terms

- **Service animals.** Damage by a guest's service animal is covered as pet damage where the level covers it as such (every level does).
- **Bodily injury and third-party liability** are never decided by support where the level does not have support handle them (no level does).
- **Appeals.** One appeal per claim, within the appeal window after the denial (30 calendar days on every level). The claims team's decision on the appeal is final. An appeal decision is recorded on the claim as a second denial entry.

## Points of judgement

- A claim filed in time but on which no guest payment request was ever sent is denied as *no guest request*, not *filed late*.
- A claim on a stay that checked in before the plan's effective date is denied as *coverage inactive*.
- A host whose appeal has been decided has used the one appeal the claim allows.
